description: Repositories for the new core tables plus the Postgres-backed background_job queue. Adds nine repository modules in the existing style (constructor takes db, methods call this.db.query), and src/jobs/jobQueue.js implementing enqueue, claim with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, markDone, markFailed with retry/attempts and run_after exponential backoff, a bounded concurrent worker loop (start/stop), plus src/jobs/handlers.js registering no-op stub handlers for the four job types. Jobs live in Postgres so they survive restart. Depends on FEAT-001 (tables + env keys must exist). Adds node:test unit coverage for the pure backoff/retry logic and repo SQL shapes. Does NOT implement later-step business logic — handlers are stubs.
steps: Read context.json and this file FIRST, plus backend/src/repositories/topicRepository.js and questionRepository.js for the repo pattern, and FEAT-001's findings for exact column names.

Create backend/src/repositories/appUserRepository.js (create, findById, findByEmail, findByCode, updateLoginState, setStatus), subjectRepository.js (create, findById, list, addLecturer, listLecturers), courseMaterialRepository.js (create, findById, listBySubject, updateStatus), questionGenerationJobRepository.js (create, findById, updateStatus, incrementGenerated), examSessionRepository.js (create, findById, list, addStudent, addExaminer, setStatus), vivaInterviewRepository.js (create, findById, findByExamAndStudent, updateProgress, setStatus), qaTurnRepository.js (create, listByInterview, update), vivaResultRepository.js (create, findByInterview, setStatus, finalize). Each takes db in the constructor and uses this.db.query(sql, params); follow the static UPDATABLE_COLUMNS whitelist + dynamic $n SET builder from topicRepository.js for update methods.

Create backend/src/repositories/backgroundJobRepository.js with enqueue(type,payload,{runAfter,maxAttempts}), findById(id), claimNext(client) issuing UPDATE background_job SET status='RUNNING', locked_at=now() WHERE job_id = (SELECT job_id FROM background_job WHERE status='PENDING' AND run_after<=now() ORDER BY run_after FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1) RETURNING *, markDone(id), markFailed(id, errorText, nextRunAfter). The claim query is the mechanism the queue relies on.

Create backend/src/jobs/jobQueue.js exporting a JobQueue class: constructor({ db, repository, env, logger }); enqueue(type,payload,opts) delegating to the repository; registerHandler(type, fn); start() running a bounded worker loop (at most env.jobQueueConcurrency in flight, polling every env.jobQueuePollIntervalMs) that claims a job inside db.withTransaction (so FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED holds for the claim), runs the handler, then markDone; on handler throw calls markFailed and, when attempts < max_attempts, re-queues with run_after = now() + computeBackoffMs(attempts) else leaves it FAILED; stop() halts the loop and waits for in-flight jobs. Export a PURE computeBackoffMs(attempt, baseMs=env default) using exponential backoff with a cap so it is unit-testable without a DB.

Create backend/src/jobs/handlers.js registering no-op stub handlers for INGEST_MATERIAL, GENERATE_QUESTIONS, GRADE_INTERVIEW, SEND_EMAIL (log via logger and resolve). Export a registerDefaultHandlers(queue, deps) helper. Do not implement real ingest/generate/grade/email logic (later steps).

Add backend/test/jobQueueService.test.js (node:test): assert computeBackoffMs is monotonic non-decreasing and capped; assert the markFailed retry-vs-FAILED decision by attempts; construct backgroundJobRepository against a fake db stub ({ query: async(sql,params)=>{...capture...} }) and assert the claim SQL contains FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and the enqueue/markDone param shapes. No real Postgres.
Run cd backend; npm test and cd backend; npm run test:e2e; confirm green with no Docker and no regression in existing tests.

- backgroundJobRepository.js -> BackgroundJobRepository: enqueue(type, payload, {runAfter, maxAttempts}) [payload JSON.stringify'd, params order: type, payloadJson, maxAttempts, runAfter], findById(id), claimNext(client) [UPDATE ... SET status='RUNNING', locked_at=now(), attempts=attempts+1 WHERE id=(SELECT ... WHERE status='PENDING' AND run_after<=now() ORDER BY run_after FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1) RETURNING *; pass a tx client to hold the row lock, falls back to this.db if no client], markDone(id), markFailed(id, errorText, nextRunAfter=null) [nextRunAfter null => status FAILED; non-null => status PENDING + run_after=nextRunAfter].

QUEUE API (backend/src/jobs/jobQueue.js, `module.exports = { JobQueue, computeBackoffMs, DEFAULT_BASE_BACKOFF_MS, DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CAP_MS }`):
- class JobQueue; constructor({ db, repository, env, logger }) — repository defaults to `new BackgroundJobRepository(db)`; reads env.jobQueueConcurrency (default 2), env.jobQueuePollIntervalMs (default 1000, also used as backoff base), env.jobMaxAttempts (default 3).
- registerHandler(type, fn) -> this (chainable).
- async enqueue(type, payload, opts={}) -> delegates to repository.enqueue, injecting maxAttempts = opts.maxAttempts ?? env.jobMaxAttempts.
- start() -> begins a bounded polling worker loop (<= concurrency in flight; setTimeout(unref) polling at pollIntervalMs); idempotent.
- async stop() -> halts loop, clears timer, awaits Promise.allSettled of in-flight jobs.
- Internals: _claim() runs repository.claimNext inside db.withTransaction(tx) so FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED holds; _process(job) runs the handler then markDone, on throw calls _handleFailure; _handleFailure re-queues via markFailed(id, msg, new Date(Date.now()+computeBackoffMs(attempts))) while job.attempts < max_attempts (falls back to env.jobMaxAttempts ?? 3), else markFailed(id, msg, null) to leave it FAILED.
- PURE `computeBackoffMs(attempt, baseMs=1000, capMs=60000)` = min(baseMs * 2**(attempt-1), capMs); monotonic non-decreasing, capped; unit-tested without a DB.

HANDLERS (backend/src/jobs/handlers.js, `module.exports = { registerDefaultHandlers, makeStubHandler }`): registerDefaultHandlers(queue, deps={}) registers NO-OP stub handlers (log + resolve) for INGEST_MATERIAL, GENERATE_QUESTIONS, GRADE_INTERVIEW, SEND_EMAIL. makeStubHandler(type, logger) returns the stub. NO real business logic — later steps (FEAT-003+) replace these.

TEST: backend/test/jobQueueService.test.js (node:test, named *Service.test.js so `node --test` picks it up) — asserts computeBackoffMs exponential/monotonic/capped, _handleFailure retry-vs-FAILED by attempts, and backgroundJobRepository SQL shapes against a fake `{query}` db stub (claim SQL contains FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; enqueue/markDone/markFailed param shapes).

FOR FEAT-003: JobQueue + registerDefaultHandlers are wired by the caller (not yet mounted in server.js — server.js was NOT modified by FEAT-002). To run the queue in production, construct `new JobQueue({ db, env, logger })`, call registerDefaultHandlers(queue, { logger }) (or registerHandler per type to override stubs with real logic), then queue.start(); call queue.stop() on shutdown. Enqueue work with queue.enqueue(type, payload, { runAfter, maxAttempts }).
